sections: Design Pillars: What is Central to the Experience?

candidate.tagline: Ex-trucker. Track boss. Pick up your butts.
candidate.description: Retired long-haul trucker who runs a dirt track in Hoon. Stubborn, mustached, and carrying a spare tire. He beats up punks who won't pick up their cigarette butts.

llm_verdict.summary: The tagline is 43 characters, over the 40-character limit, which is a blocking issue. The id, display_name and description are valid. The description is about 163 characters in three sentences, and its facts match the GDD and Style Guide. The description's tone is a bit flat, but that is a minor point.

issues.quote: Ex-trucker. Track boss. Pick up your butts.
issues.explanation: the tagline is 43 characters; the UI limit is at most 40.
issues.recommendation: Rewrite the tagline to at most 40 characters.

issues.quote: Ex-trucker. Track boss. Pick up your butts.
issues.explanation: The task caps the tagline at 40 characters. This one is 43 (11 + 1 + 11 + 1 + 19), so it violates the stated limit.
issues.recommendation: Cut at least 3 characters. For example, drop 'Track boss.' and use 'Ex-trucker. Pick up your butts.' (about 31 characters), or shorten the line another way and keep it at 40 or under.

issues.quote: Stubborn, mustached, and carrying a spare tire.
issues.explanation: This is accurate to the Style Guide, but it reads as a plain list. It lacks the dark, irreverent Southern bite the GDD's Tone & Aesthetics section calls for. It also leans on the physical look rather than his temperament.
issues.recommendation: Optionally give it more attitude within the documented facts. For example, play up his stubbornness and his habit of intimidating anyone who causes trouble near his trailer.

issues.explanation: The line is funny, but out of context 'butts' can be read as a bare crude joke. The documented gag is specifically about cigarette butts.
issues.recommendation: Consider making the cigarette-butt reference clearer, as long as the line still fits the 40-character limit.

candidate.tagline: Pick up your cigarette butts. Or else.
candidate.description: Retired long-haul trucker who runs a dirt track in Hoon. Stubborn as a stuck axle, and he'll intimidate anyone who causes trouble near his trailer. Litter your butts and he'll beat you up.

llm_verdict.summary: No blocking issues. The id and display_name are correct. The tagline is about 38 characters and the description is about 187, both within limits. Every fact traces to the GDD profile: retired long-haul trucker, dirt track in Hoon, stubborn, intimidates troublemakers near his trailer, and beats up punks who leave cigarette butts. Nothing is invented, and no out-of-scope mechanics appear. Tone is on target, with two minor polish notes.

issues.quote: Litter your butts and he'll beat you up.
issues.explanation: "Litter your butts" is awkward phrasing. The line also repeats the tagline's cigarette-butt joke, so it adds little. The GDD's phrasing is "neighborhood punks", and the line is flatter than the dark Southern humor the Tone section calls for.
issues.recommendation: Replace it with a sharper, non-repeating line, for example one that nods to the neighborhood punks or his mustache-and-cutoffs trucker attitude. Keep it within 220 characters total.

issues.quote: Retired long-haul trucker who runs a dirt track in Hoon.
issues.explanation: The description makes no direct reference to Barry's appearance or his "Hot Potato" persona. It would be a bit more distinctive with a Style Guide look cue. This is optional, and the task did not require it.
issues.recommendation: Optionally work in one Style Guide look detail, such as the Wild Bill mustache or the cutoff jean shorts, if space allows.

final.tagline: Pick up your cigarette butts. Or else.
final.description: Retired long-haul trucker who runs a dirt track in Hoon. Stubborn as a stuck axle, and he'll intimidate anyone who causes trouble near his trailer. Litter your butts and he'll beat you up.

candidate.description: Trailer-park goth, expelled at sixteen. Years of roughhousing with his football-playing brothers taught him to take a beating. He wears eyeliner, not eye black, and he's sick of loudmouth rednecks.

llm_verdict.summary: The candidate has no blocking issues. The id and display_name are correct. The tagline is about 27 characters, under the 40 limit. The description is about 197 characters in three short sentences, inside the 80-220 range. The facts match the GDD and Style Guide: goth, expelled at sixteen, football-playing brothers, eyeliner over eye black, and no patience for rednecks. It invents no mechanics, titles or biography. The tone is on target, though plain in places.

issues.quote: He wears eyeliner, not eye black, and he's sick of loudmouth rednecks.
issues.explanation: The description never mentions backyard wrestling, which the task asked it to reflect. The tone is also a bit tame next to the dark, irreverent Southern humor in the GDD.
issues.recommendation: Optionally work in the backyard wrestling and add a sharper, darker line. Keep the length under 220 characters and don't add any new biography.

issues.explanation: The GDD says his older brothers played college football. The text is not wrong, but it drops that detail.

final.description: Trailer-park goth, expelled at sixteen. Years of roughhousing with his football-playing brothers taught him to take a beating. He wears eyeliner, not eye black, and he's sick of loudmouth rednecks.

messages.text: Pick up your cigarette butts on the way out, Peaux.
Hot Potato's still hot. Stay down, punk.
Nap time, Peaux. I got a dirt track to run.
Back to the trailer. Beer's getting warm.
My brothers hit harder than that, Barry. Way harder.
Stay down, redneck. Quiet's nice for once.
Expelled at sixteen. Still smarter than you, Barry.

llm_verdict.summary: No blocking issues. All 8 lines (4 per wrestler) use valid ids "barry" and "peaux" and are well under 90 characters. They have no placeholders or braces. Each fits a knockout win and invents no mechanic. The details come from the GDD: Barry's cigarette-butt grudge, his dirt track and beer gut, and Peaux's eyeliner, older brothers and expulsion at sixteen. Opponents are named by first name only. The tone is dark, irreverent Southern trailer-park humor, and the two wrestlers' lines are similar in style and length.
